**Searching for main page scrollbar****Identifying scrollbar color variable**

I'm checking App.global.css for the --border variable definition and inspecting ScrollArea.tsx to confirm use of the bg-border class tied to the scrollbar thumb color. I'll get exact file paths and line numbers next.**Identifying scrollbar thumb styling**

The scrollbar thumb uses the CSS variable `--border` defined in `App.global.css` root and dark themes. If using the ScrollArea component, the thumb's `bg-border` class also references this variable. I'll provide links with approximate line numbers to these CSS definitions.**Confirming scrollbar thumb styling and references**

The scrollbar thumb color uses the `--border` CSS variable defined in `App.global.css` (:root at line 16 and .dark at line 47). The ScrollArea component’s thumb has class `bg-border` (around line 45 in `ScrollArea.tsx`), also referencing `--border`. The global webkit scrollbar (around line 97 in `App.global.css`) uses `--border` as well. If the main page uses the native scrollbar instead of ScrollArea, it still uses the same `--border` variable for the thumb color.Yes. The scrollbar thumb/slider color comes from the `--border` CSS variable, and the scroll thumb uses it.

Where it’s set:
- `--border` for light/dark themes: `undefined`
- Global scrollbar thumb uses `--border`: `undefined`
- The custom ScrollArea thumb uses `bg-border` (which maps to `--border`): `undefined`

If the Main page uses the custom `ScrollArea`, it inherits `bg-border`. If it uses the native scrollbar, it uses the global `::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb` and `scrollbar-color` tied to `--border`.

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import * as ScrollAreaPrimitive from '@radix-ui/react-scroll-area';

import { cn } from '@houdoku/ui/util';

interface ScrollAreaProps extends React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root> {
  viewportRef?: React.Ref<HTMLDivElement>;
}

const ScrollArea = React.forwardRef<
  React.ElementRef<typeof ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root>,
  ScrollAreaProps
>(({ className, children, viewportRef, ...props }, ref) => (
  <ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root
    ref={ref}
    className={cn('relative overflow-hidden', className)}
    {...props}
  >
    <ScrollAreaPrimitive.Viewport ref={viewportRef} className="h-full w-full rounded-[inherit]">
      {children}
    </ScrollAreaPrimitive.Viewport>
    <ScrollBar />
    <ScrollAreaPrimitive.Corner />
  </ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root>
));
ScrollArea.displayName = ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root.displayName;

const ScrollBar = React.forwardRef<
  React.ElementRef<typeof ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaScrollbar>,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaScrollbar>
>(({ className, orientation = 'vertical', ...props }, ref) => (
  <ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaScrollbar
    ref={ref}
    orientation={orientation}
    className={cn(
      'flex touch-none select-none transition-colors',
      orientation === 'vertical' && 'h-full w-2.5 border-l border-l-transparent p-[1px]',
      orientation === 'horizontal' && 'h-2.5 flex-col border-t border-t-transparent p-[1px]',
      className,
    )}
    {...props}
  >
    <ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaThumb className="relative flex-1 rounded-full bg-[hsl(var(--scrollbar-thumb))]" />
  </ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaScrollbar>
));
ScrollBar.displayName = ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaScrollbar.displayName;

export { ScrollArea, ScrollBar };

```

**Adding CSS variable for scrollbar thumb**

I'm adding a new --scrollbar-thumb CSS variable in global styles and applying it in ScrollArea.tsx's scrollbar thumb using Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax with hsl(var(--scrollbar-thumb)). This ensures consistent theming with the existing border color variable.Yes. I added a new CSS variable `--scrollbar-thumb` and wired it to both native scrollbars and the custom `ScrollArea` thumb.

Set the value here:
- Light/Dark defaults: `undefined`

Used here:
- Native scrollbar thumb + Firefox color: `undefined`
- Custom `ScrollArea` thumb: `undefined`

Change `--scrollbar-thumb` to any HSL triplet (e.g., `0 0% 60%`) to adjust only the thumb color.
